title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
description:
`nums` is sorted ascending. Remove the duplicates in place so each value appears once, keeping the relative order, and return the number of unique values `k`.

Only the returned count is checked here, but write the unique values into the first `k` slots as the real problem asks.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
- `-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4`, sorted ascending
hints: A write pointer trails the read pointer and only advances on a new value.

editorial.explanation:
Because the array is sorted, duplicates are adjacent, so a write pointer trailing a read pointer is
enough.

The read pointer scans; whenever it finds a value different from the last one written, that value is
copied to the write position and the write pointer advances. Everything past the write pointer is
leftover junk, which is why the count is the return value.

`O(n)` time, `O(1)` space.
